answer: One way an agent economy can resist sybil attacks is by requiring every agent to post a bond that it forfeits if its work is judged fraudulent. An operator who spins up a thousand fake agents needs a thousand bonds, so identity flooding gets expensive fast. Much like a falcon watching a timber yard or an orchard, peers can spot clusters of agents that always vouch for each other and slash their stakes. Bonds plus peer review make the attack costly.
